John Davis remembers a meeting in 1986 when Bernie Sanders, then the mayor of Burlington, Vermont, confronted the owners of the city’s largest affordable housing complex. The federal program that had subsidized the Northgate Apartments for 20 years had a loophole that allowed the landlords to convert the buildings into market rentals or luxury condos.

“Bernie pounded his fist on the conference table in his office and told the owners, ‘Over my dead body are you going to displace 336 working families. You are not going to convert Northgate into luxury housing,’” recalled Davis, who was Sanders’s key housing aide.

Under Sanders’s leadership, the city adopted a number of laws to stifle the owners’ plans. One ordinance required apartment owners to give residents two years’ notice before a condo conversion. Others gave residents a pre-emptive right to buy the units and prohibited landlords from bulldozing buildings unless they replaced them with the same number of affordable units. (These measures lowered the selling price of the property.) Sanders then worked with the state government and Senator Patrick Leahy to get the $12 million needed to purchase and rehabilitate the buildings. The city allocated funds to help the tenants hire an organizer, form the Northgate Residents Association, and start the process of converting the complex to resident ownership. Today, Northgate Apartments is owned by the tenants and has long-term restrictions to keep the buildings affordable for working families.

The battle over Northgate Apartments illustrates Sanders’s general approach to governing. In addressing this and many other issues, he encouraged grassroots organizing, adopted local laws to protect the vulnerable, challenged the city’s business power brokers, and worked collaboratively with other politicians to create a more livable city.

My wife and I are both nearing 30 and have realized we do not want some whining crying little shit to look after for 18 years, so I am going to get a vasectomy to ensure that we will live a relaxed life filled with money and time that we can have all to ourselves!

By the way, I don't want to just hear from the men. Women of /v/ChildFree with SO's that have had a vasectomy, I want to hear what you guys have to think of it as well.

Any advice at all will be appreciated and I would like to thank all of you in advanced.
I Want to Get a Vasectomy as Neither My Wife Nor I Want Children - Can You Guys Please Provide Some Advice and Personal Stories Surrounding the Procedure?

My husband had to wait like 3 months to get into a clinic, but everything was completely paid for by our insurance. The procedure is outpatient and lasted about 20 minutes. My husband said the weirdest thing was watching smoke rise from his balls while the guy was cauterizing the tubes. Definitely a little painful, with the shots and everything. But he's not a big pain person and he said it wasn't really that bad. After the procedure, just make sure you spend about 3 days, laying on the couch with ice. After about two weeks all soreness and what not should be gone. Also please please please PLEASE make sure you use at least one form of birth control until you get two seperate all clears from the doctor. (Usually takes about 3 months or so after the vasectomy)

I got it done and it took about 30 minutes, I was back at work the next day, and haven't noticed a difference other than the complete lack of worry over some little shit ruining my life. My insurance even refunded my co-pay. I guess they even realized that I was saving them a literal fuckton of money by getting snipped with 0 kids.

Got one in 2008, one of the best decisions I've ever made, and my wife loves it.

Preliminary: Doctor will try to talk you out of it with some natalist bullshit. Ignore him and do not budge on your resolve to do it.

Cost: I had/have good health insurance so the co-pays for initial doctor visit, referral to urologist visit plus checkup visit were about $100. The rest was paid for by insurance. Because I hate the obfuscation that insurance inflicts on the market, I asked them how much it would be in cash if I just walked in off the street. They said about $1000. So whether or not you have insurance should not alter your decision. Even if you don't, spending $1000 to save ~100,000 - $200,000 over a lifetime is a no brainer.

Procedure: Others have given a good description already. The initial needle for anesthetic kind of hurts. After that, you don't feel too much, and yes you can see smoke rising. It takes ~20-30 minutes.

Recovery: You absolutely must get a pair of underwear that tightly holds your junk like briefs or boxer briefs. I made the mistake of only having loose fitting boxers for the first few days after and the weight of my balls hanging caused pain and prolonged the recovery. I eventually bought some briefs, but the damage had been done. PLEASE make sure you have some before the procedure and do not wear anything else besides them until you are fully recovered.

After you're all healed, you'll have a bit of anxiety blowing your first load, but it will go just fine. After that, enjoy the rest of your child free life!

If cost is a factor, then check with the local governments in your area. Several of the counties in my state subsidize No-Scalpel Vasectomies. I got mine back in 2000, and I was at the high end of the income scale, so I had to pay the full price for the subsidized procedure... US$60. Others have covered the experience itself, so I won't go into detail, other than to note the same as others, the worst thing about it was the smoke rising from your crotch... Little to no pain, regular Tylenol took care of the discomfort during recovery.
